mechanism_narrative: Because WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rebounded in the latest week after a sharp dip, commuter-driven weekday foot traffic should lift RETAIL_REC over the next month. If the rebound persists, retail visits will move in the same direction within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -51.6 to -46.3 and TRANSIT improved from -42.3 to -39.1 in t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep rising for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days, reject the commuter-footfall mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The latest improvement in RESIDENTIAL after a strong stay-at-home pattern implies more time spent near home and less discretionary shopping travel, which should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive at 9.4 in t-0w after 9.7 in t-1w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 9 for the next two weeks and RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean, this stay-at-home suppression hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed drop in GROCERY_PHARM below its prior month signals tighter local errands and substitution toward essential trips, which will also suppress discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -20 after being above -18
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell to -21.4 in t-1w before partially recovering to -16.6 in t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above -20 for the next month and RETAIL_REC still rises versus the prior 28 days, the essential-trip suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility weakens while TRANSIT does not, outdoor leisure absorbs less weekend demand and indoor shopping recovers more slowly. In that regime, RETAIL_REC should remain below its recent average over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -8 while TRANSIT stays below -35
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -3.6 to -9.6 and then to -7.9 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS remains below -8 and TRANSIT below -35 for a week but RETAIL_REC jumps above its last-4-week mean, the leisure-substitution claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates fewer access frictions and more downtown circulation, which will translate into higher retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES rises by at least 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in t-0w after weakening in t-1w
failure_condition: If the specified rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT occurs but RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean within 28 days, reject the access-friction mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES falls faster than TRANSIT, office-day normalization is breaking and retail spillovers weaken. That relative labor-market slack should push RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops more than TRANSIT on a week-over-week basis
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -45.4 to -51.6 while TRANSIT only moved from -39.3 to -42.3 in t-1w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES keeps falling faster than TRANSIT but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days, the office-day spillover hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp deterioration in PARKS mobility below the recent range is a proxy for stronger mobility restraint or adverse conditions, which will spill over into lower discretionary retail movement in the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -3.6 to -9.6 before recovering slightly to -7.9
failure_condition: If PARKS falls below -10 and remains there for at least one week but RETAIL_REC still increases over the next 28 days, reject the restraint-spillover hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL move together, routine neighborhood activity is replacing discretionary trips. That combination should keep RETAIL_REC subdued over the next four weeks, especially if both series stay near their current levels.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is still negative while RESIDENTIAL is persistently positive
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stabilizes near its current level and RESIDENTIAL stays positive, yet RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean within 28 days, the neighborhood-routine suppression mechanism fails.
